LOOK (Efeonce photographic language v2): premium editorial business photography, like a feature story in a top business magazine. Shot on a full-frame camera. Natural, true-to-life color exactly as the scene looks, rich clean blacks, clean highlights, soft natural contrast; no color grading, no filter, no teal-and-orange, no HDR, no added grain. Motivated, directional light: soft window light from one side, gentle modeling on faces, never flat, never flash. Restraint and calm: few objects, noble real materials (oak wood, linen, paper, brushed metal), uncluttered. Real skin texture and real fabric, no retouching look. People genuinely working together, mid-conversation, not looking at the camera, no stock smiles, no handshakes, no thumbs up. Contemporary Santiago de Chile professional setting, specific and lived-in, not a generic glass office. No text, no letters, no logos, no watermarks anywhere.

POINT OF VIEW (essential): the photograph is taken from the CLIENT'S OWN SEAT at the table. The camera sits where the client sits, so the viewer is placed inside the working session.

SCENE (vertical 4:5): A working session in a meeting room with large windows, soft overcast daylight from the left. Across the oak table, a Chilean strategist in her late thirties, wearing a plain deep navy polo with no logo, explains something while turning a laptop slightly toward the camera and gesturing with an open hand; next to her a colleague in his thirties listens and takes notes in a paper notebook. The laptop screen shows a clean abstract dashboard with soft blue and grey shapes, no legible text or numbers. Camera: 85mm lens at f/2, positioned low at table height from the client's seat, focus on the strategist's eyes. FOREGROUND (planned, part of the point of view): the bottom 18% of the frame is the NEAR EDGE OF THE CLIENT'S OWN SIDE OF THE OAK TABLE, a calm, empty, continuous wooden surface running across the ENTIRE width of the frame, completely out of focus, smooth and soft, with no objects on it. Composition: the two people occupy the middle band; the upper quarter is the softly out-of-focus wall and window light.
